summary_insights: Revenue grew by 8.6% year-on-year, rising from £769,931 to £836,440.
Net profit increased significantly by 31.6%, driven by a reduction in administrative overheads.
Gross margin experienced a slight compression, falling from 35.0% to 33.7% due to rising direct labour costs.
Administrative expenses were reduced by 14.2%, largely due to a sharp decrease in advertising and marketing spend (down 73%).
Directors' remuneration was reduced by 17.5%, contributing to improved bottom-line performance.
Interest coverage ratio improved from 112x to 204x, indicating exceptionally strong financial resilience and low debt risk.
The company paid out £104,000 in dividends during 2024, which exceeded the year's net profit of £99,753.
Overall profitability is trending upwards with net margin expanding from 9.9% to 11.9%.
The company maintains a healthy liquidity position with a current ratio of 1.98, although this has tightened from 2.28 in the prior year.
Net assets decreased by 4.7% from £89,747 to £85,500, primarily driven by a substantial dividend distribution of £104,000 which exceeded the year's profit of £99,753.
The tangible asset base reduced by 24.7% due to depreciation and disposals of computer equipment, with minimal new investment during the period.
Trade debtors increased significantly by 185% (£8,205 to £23,387), which may indicate a slowdown in payment collections or a recent surge in sales activity.
Long-term leverage has improved, with the gearing ratio falling from 28.3% to 19.2% as bank loans are steadily repaid.
Working capital remains positive at £89,706, providing a solid buffer for short-term operational requirements.
The company is heavily reliant on 'Other Debtors' (£76,739), which represents a significant portion of the current asset mix and warrants further investigation into recoverability.
The business remains profitable with a profit for the financial year of £99,753, up 31.6% from the previous year's £75,822.
